fieldissues.issue: The medium uses editorial labels such as “gangster extortion,” “rhetorical hostage,” and “collective punishment,” then adds an internal archive rationale. The long description says the sources document a threat but do not establish a war-crime finding or collective punishment.

“collective punishment language” can read as a legal characterization that the long description expressly says is not established; “infrastructure threat” and “military threats” substantially overlap.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Trump threatened to attack Iranian power plants if Iran did not reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his deadline, according to AP. The supplied reports document the threat, not an attack carried out under it.”

Remove “collective punishment language” and consolidate “infrastructure threat” with “military threats.” Retain focused subjects such as “Strait of Hormuz,” “Iran war,” and “threat to power infrastructure.”

evidencebasis: The supplied long description attributes the reported threat to AP, says no attack under the ultimatum is documented, and states that the packet does not establish a war-crime finding or collective punishment. Both AP URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-2108. The title is specific and the long description adds legal and factual context without presenting the threat as an implemented attack.

fieldissues.issue: “Trump’s Student-Loan Chaos Left Millions Without a Clear Way to Pay” makes a broad causal claim about millions; the long description says borrowers had difficulty finding guidance and cautions that it does not establish every borrower was unable to pay.
The medium uses evaluative terms such as “cruelty,” “institutional sabotage,” and “the harm,” rather than summarizing the reported uncertainty in repayment guidance.
“trump chaos” is an editorial label, and “public welfare harm” repeats the subcategory instead of naming a subject.

proposedchanges.change: Replace with: “Borrowers face uncertainty over federal student-loan repayment options.”
Replace with: “The Guardian reported confusion over repayment options after court challenges to the SAVE plan and changes to federal loan forms left borrowers seeking clear guidance.”
Remove “trump chaos” and the duplicated “public welfare harm” label. Retain “student loans,” “SAVE plan,” and “borrower confusion,” and add “repayment options” if desired.

evidencebasis: The supplied long description connects borrower uncertainty to court challenges and later removal of online forms, while stating that not every borrower was unable to pay and that one policy did not cause all servicing problems. Both Guardian URLs are retained.
notes: Existing entry-2119. Keep the account’s qualification about the number of affected borrowers and the causal limits.

fieldissues.issue: The title and preserved long description state that the administration required database access, conditioned DHS grants, and carried out mass disenfranchisement. The packet’s medium says the linked materials do not document such a requirement or implementation.

The metadata presents systematic voter suppression, federal coercion, and agency involvement as established, but the packet only supports concern about potential Project 2025 effects on voting rights and election administration.

proposedchanges.change: Until the packet includes evidence of an adopted policy and implementation, revise the title to “Project 2025 proposals raise voting-rights concerns” and limit the long description to potential effects described in the supplied materials. Remove claims of required data sharing, grant conditions, targeted purges, and affected groups unless supported.

Remove the specific suppression and agency-enforcement labels unless supported. Use only neutral subjects from the supplied materials, such as “Project 2025,” “voting rights,” and “election administration”; do not tag DHS or DOJ as implementing actors without packet evidence.

evidencebasis: The supplied medium explicitly says the linked materials discuss potential effects but do not document the alleged database requirement or mass purges. The long field repeats those unverified claims. The three Common Cause and civil-rights source URLs remain present.
notes: Existing entry-213. The medium already signals the evidence gap; the title, long text, and metadata need packet-level resolution before release.

The medium repeats the packet’s evaluative commentary (“too on-brand” and “part of the show”) rather than the documented ceremony and Trump’s remarks.
“War-as-Spectacle,” “war spectacle,” and “trump optics” imply an intent or effect the long description expressly says the report does not establish.
